title: ISC Civic Science Fellow 2026: Fully Funded Remote Fellowship Offering a $5,000 Monthly Stipend for Early- to Mid-Career Researchers
summary: Scientific evidence is essential for solving many of the world s most pressing challenges, from climate change and public health to technological innovation and sustainable development. However, producing quality scientific research is only part of the solution. Equally important is ensuring that scientific evidence is communicated effectively so that policymakers, governments, international organizations, and society can understand, trust, and act upon it. To strengthen this critical connection between science and policy, the International Science Council (ISC) has opened applications for its prestigious ISC Civic Science Fellow 2026 . This fully funded, 18-month Fellowship provides an exceptional opportunity for outstanding early- to mid-career researchers who are passionate about science communication, public engagement, and evidence-informed policymaking. Hosted virtually by the International Science Council, the Fellowship enables researchers to work directly with one of the world s leading science organizations while contributing to innovative research that improves the communication of scientific evidence in international policy processes. The Fellowship is funded through the Rita Allen Civic Science Fellows Program , offering participants a monthly stipend of approximately USD 5,000 , international networking opportunities, and the chance to influence how scientific evidence informs global decision-making. About the International Science Council Civic Science Fellowship The ISC Civic Science Fellowship is designed for researchers who want to bridge the gap between science and policymaking by improving how scientific evidence is communicated across complex international environments. Today s policy decisions are increasingly influenced by scientific research. Yet communicating scientific evidence effectively within multilateral institutions remains challenging due to political, institutional, social, and cultural factors that affect how information is interpreted and utilized. This Fellowship addresses these challenges by enabling researchers to investigate communication strategies, develop practical tools, and strengthen the role of science in international governance. Throughout the Fellowship, participants will work closely with: The International Science Council Secretariat Global scientific organizations International partners Communication professionals Policymakers Scientists International organizations Academic researchers The goal is to identify and implement more effective ways of communicating scientific evidence to support better policymaking around the world. Fellowship Overview Fellowship Detail Information Fellowship Duration 18 Months Host Organization International Science Council (ISC) Location Remote (Virtual) Possible Travel Yes, including visits to Paris and selected UN locations Start Date September 2026 Funding Fully Funded Monthly Stipend Approximately USD 5,000 Funding Provider Rita Allen Civic Science Fellows Program Application Deadline 16 August 2026 Why This Fellowship Matters Scientific research alone does not automatically influence public policy. Many global decisions are shaped by: Political priorities Institutional processes Public trust Communication quality Cultural differences Information ecosystems Digital media environments Public perception Misinformation and disinformation As a result, scientific evidence often struggles to reach decision-makers in ways that are understandable, trusted, and actionable. The ISC Civic Science Fellowship seeks to address these challenges by helping researchers understand how science can be communicated more effectively within international governance systems. Participants will contribute to real-world research while developing practical guidance that can improve science communication worldwide. Fellowship Responsibilities During the 18-month Fellowship, participants will contribute to a wide range of research and engagement activities. These include: 1. Mapping Existing Science Communication Practices The Fellow will: Examine current communication approaches used by international organizations. Study communication channels. Analyze audience engagement strategies. Identify effective communication models across different organizations. 2. Conducting Research on Scientific Information Ecosystems Participants will investigate: How scientific evidence is communicated. How audiences interpret scientific information. Factors influencing evidence uptake. The role of institutional and political environments. 3. Identifying Barriers to Evidence-Based Decision-Making Research activities include examining: Obstacles preventing scientific evidence from influencing policy. Institutional challenges. Communication gaps. Trust issues. Cultural considerations. 4. Studying Digital Information Environments The Fellow will analyze how evolving digital platforms influence science communication, including: Misinformation Disinformation Digital media Online engagement Public information behavior 5. Applying Behavioural and Social Science Participants will use evidence from: Behavioural science Psychology Communication studies Social sciences to identify more effective approaches for communicating scientific evidence to diverse audiences. 6. Developing Practical Communication Resources The Fellow will help create: Communication toolkits Practical guidance Best practice documents Evidence communication frameworks Resources for scientific organizations 7. Testing New Communication Approaches Working alongside ISC initiatives, the Fellow will: Pilot communication strategies. Evaluate their effectiveness. Recommend improvements. 8. Producing Publications Expected outputs include: Research reports Policy briefs Analytical papers Guidance documents Publications for international audiences 9. Supporting International Networks The Fellow will contribute to: Academic engagement Stakeholder outreach International collaborations Professional networking Who Should Apply? The Fellowship is particularly suited for researchers interested in: Science communication Public engagement with science Trust in science Behavioural science Evidence-informed policymaking Public policy International governance Civic science Decision-making research Information ecosystems Applicants passionate about understanding how people engage with scientific evidence and how scientific knowledge shapes society are especially encouraged to apply. Eligibility Requirements Applicants must satisfy all of the following requirements: Hold a PhD or expect to complete one before September 2026. Be available full-time throughout the 18-month Fellowship. Obtain employer support if currently employed. Sign the required agreements with the ISC and the Rita Allen Foundation. Possess a valid passport. Be eligible for international travel and visas. Participate in weekly Tuesday Learning Labs from noon to 2:00 pm ET. Be available to begin the Fellowship in September 2026. Desired Skills and Experience Strong applicants should demonstrate: Excellent research experience. High-quality academic publications. Expertise in science communication. Experience working with governments or international organizations. Ability to translate research into policy guidance. Outstanding written and spoken English. Strong communication and facilitation skills. Ability to work independently in international environments. Additional desirable experience includes: International collaborations. Interdisciplinary research. Capacity-building initiatives. Work within multilateral organizations. Relevant Academic Fields Researchers from a variety of disciplines are encouraged to apply, including: Behavioural Science Cognitive Science Psychology Science Communication Political Science Public Policy Risk Analysis Decision Science Individual and Collective Action Research Fellowship Benefits Successful Fellows will receive numerous professional and financial benefits, including: Financial Support Fully funded Fellowship. Monthly stipend of approximately USD 5,000 . Funding through the Rita Allen Civic Science Fellows Program. Career Development Participants will: Conduct high-impact applied research. Work with globally recognized scientific organizations. Gain experience in international science policy. Strengthen leadership skills. Enhance science communication expertise. International Exposure Fellows will have opportunities to: Collaborate with experts worldwide. Participate in international meetings. Attend workshops and conferences. Visit the ISC headquarters in Paris. Engage with United Nations-related activities. Professional Networking Participants will become part of an international network of: Scientists Science communicators Policy experts Journalists Researchers International organizations Long-Term Impact The Fellowship enables participants to contribute to global resources that improve science communication and evidence-informed policymaking for scientific organizations around the world. Why You Should Apply This Fellowship offers much more than financial support. It provides an opportunity to: Influence international science policy. Work alongside globally recognized experts. Build an international professional network. Improve public understanding of science. Help combat misinformation and disinformation. Develop practical tools that support evidence-based policymaking. Gain valuable experience working across science, communication, and governance. For researchers passionate about making science more accessible and impactful, this Fellowship represents an exceptional career opportunity. How to Apply Interested candidates should complete the official online application form provided by the International Science Council HERE Also, read more using same link. Applicants should ensure that all required documents are submitted before the application deadline and carefully review the eligibility criteria before applying. Conclusion The ISC Civic Science Fellow 2026 is an outstanding opportunity for early- to mid-career researchers seeking to shape the future of science communication and international policymaking. Through fully funded support, a generous monthly stipend, international collaboration, and direct engagement with leading scientific and policy organizations, Fellows will gain invaluable experience while contributing to the advancement of evidence-informed decision-making worldwide. If you have a passion for science communication, interdisciplinary research, and global policy engagement, this Fellowship offers a unique platform to develop your expertise, expand your international network, and make a lasting impact on how scientific evidence is communicated and used across the world. title: AEIP Scholars Programme 2026–2027: Fully Sponsored Africa-Europe Research Collaboration Programme for Young Scholars
summary: The AEIP Scholars Programme 2026–2027 is now accepting applications from outstanding young researchers across Africa and Europe who are passionate about advancing research, innovation, and international collaboration. The programme offers an exceptional opportunity for emerging scholars to work across continents, co-create practical research solutions, strengthen academic partnerships, and contribute to addressing some of the world s most pressing shared challenges. Launched by the Africa-Europe Innovation Platform (AEIP) , the Scholars Programme is a collaborative research initiative designed to foster stronger scientific cooperation between Africa and Europe. Through peer learning, joint research, innovation, and science communication, the programme empowers scholars to translate academic research into practical solutions that create meaningful impact for communities, institutions, women, and youth. Successful applicants will become part of a highly selective international cohort and collaborate directly with scholars from another continent while receiving the opportunity to showcase their research at the prestigious AEIP Stakeholder Meeting in Europe in June 2027 . Applications are currently open and will close on 31 August 2026 . What is the AEIP Scholars Programme? The AEIP Scholars Programme is a collaborative research impact programme that connects emerging scholars from Africa and Europe to encourage interdisciplinary research and strengthen long-term cooperation between both regions. Rather than conducting research independently, selected participants will be paired with scholars from another continent to jointly develop innovative, solution-driven research outputs based on their existing work. The programme focuses on transforming academic knowledge into practical innovations capable of addressing shared challenges facing both Africa and Europe. It also encourages scholars to expand their international networks while developing skills in: Collaborative research Research impact Innovation Science communication International partnership building Knowledge exchange Cross-cultural academic collaboration Programme Objectives The AEIP Scholars Programme seeks to strengthen collaboration between African and European researchers by supporting research that aligns with the AU-EU Innovation Agenda , particularly its Capacities for Science Action . The programme aims to: Foster collaborative research between Africa and Europe Encourage innovation through interdisciplinary partnerships Promote knowledge exchange between scholars Strengthen long-term academic cooperation Support practical research addressing global challenges Develop innovative solutions with measurable societal impact Increase science communication capacity Build stronger international research networks Understanding the AU-EU Innovation Agenda The Scholars Programme is built around the Capacities for Science Action under the AU-EU Innovation Agenda. This initiative seeks to strengthen scientific cooperation by supporting: Collaboration between African and European universities Partnerships among research institutions Joint innovation activities Academic exchange programmes Knowledge transfer initiatives Learning mobility opportunities Research collaborations addressing socioeconomic challenges Joint training programmes Recognition of higher education qualifications Academic and professional mobility Curriculum development Capacity building for students, researchers and postdoctoral fellows Digital education systems Digital transformation Digital skills development Youth employability Reducing talent drain Inclusive innovation ecosystems Through the Scholars Programme, participants contribute directly to these international objectives. How the Programme Works The programme follows a structured collaborative model. Step 1: Selection A total of 10 scholars will be selected. Participants will come from both: Africa Europe Step 2: Scholar Pairing Each scholar will be paired with another participant from the opposite continent. This creates: Five Africa-Europe research pairs Pairing is based on: Shared research interests Complementary expertise Similar academic themes Step 3: Collaborative Research Each Africa-Europe scholar pair will work together to: Develop a collaborative research activity Produce a joint research output Design a practical innovation based on their research The emphasis is on creating research that delivers real-world solutions rather than remaining purely theoretical. Step 4: Expert Evaluation The completed research outputs will be evaluated by an expert panel. Projects will be reviewed according to several criteria, including: Innovation Practicality Scalability Social impact Research quality Step 5: Final Pitching Event The top-performing scholar pairs will present their research solutions through a competitive pitching process. The three highest-ranked teams will become finalists. Step 6: AEIP Stakeholder Meeting Finalist teams will receive sponsorship to attend the AEIP Stakeholder Meeting in Europe in June 2027 , where they will showcase their collaborative research to stakeholders, experts, and innovation leaders. Evaluation Criteria Applications submitted during the selection stage will be assessed based on: Relevance of the research Academic excellence Innovation potential Alignment with Africa-Europe cooperation priorities During the collaborative phase, proposed solutions will be evaluated according to: Impact on women and youth Ability to strengthen communities and institutions Strength of the proposed solution Technology-driven innovation Practical feasibility Realistic implementation potential Expected Programme Outcomes The AEIP Scholars Programme aims to generate long-term impact by producing: Collaborative Africa-Europe research outputs Innovative practical solutions Stronger international academic partnerships Enhanced research capacity Improved knowledge exchange Sustainable development initiatives Inclusive innovation ecosystems Cross-border scientific collaboration Benefits of the AEIP Scholars Programme Selected scholars will enjoy numerous academic and professional benefits, including: Opportunity to collaborate internationally with leading young researchers Cross-continental research partnerships Peer learning opportunities Enhanced research visibility International networking Innovation development experience Science communication skills Exposure to expert reviewers Opportunity to present research before international stakeholders Sponsored participation at the AEIP Stakeholder Meeting in Europe (for finalist teams) Increased career development opportunities Contribution to solving shared global challenges Who Can Apply? The programme welcomes applications from young scholars who satisfy all eligibility requirements. Applicants must: Be between 25 and 35 years old Be based in Africa or Europe Be enrolled in a PhD , Postdoctoral programme , or further studies during the application period Have ongoing or completed: Research projects Theses Dissertations Their research must align with the AU-EU Innovation Agenda Capacities for Science Action . Application Requirements Interested applicants must submit an Expression of Interest that includes an abstract of their research. The submitted abstract should demonstrate: Research relevance Academic quality Innovation Potential impact Alignment with Africa-Europe priorities Programme Timeline July – August 2026 Applications open Programme officially launched 31 August 2026 Application deadline September 2026 Selection of 10 scholars Africa-Europe scholar pairing September 2026 – March 2027 Collaborative research period Development of joint research outputs First Half of April 2027 Evaluation of submitted projects Selection of the top three scholar pairs June 2027 AEIP Stakeholder Meeting in Europe Final presentations by the top three scholar pairs How to Apply Eligible applicants should submit their Expression of Interest through the official Africa-Europe Innovation Platform application process before the application deadline. Applicants are encouraged to carefully prepare a strong research abstract that clearly demonstrates: Originality Research excellence Practical relevance Innovation potential Alignment with the AU-EU Innovation Agenda Early applications are strongly recommended. APPLY NOW Need Assistance? For programme enquiries, applicants may contact: Email: info@africaeuropeinnovation.net When contacting the organisers, include Scholars Programme in the subject line. Application Deadline 31 August 2026 Late applications are unlikely to be considered. Interested scholars are encouraged to submit their Expression of Interest well before the deadline. Conclusion The AEIP Scholars Programme 2026–2027 offers an outstanding opportunity for emerging researchers from Africa and Europe to collaborate across borders, transform academic research into practical solutions, and strengthen international scientific partnerships. By combining innovation, knowledge exchange, and interdisciplinary collaboration, the programme prepares the next generation of scholars to address global challenges while expanding their academic and professional networks. For young researchers seeking international exposure, collaborative research experience, and the opportunity to contribute to meaningful innovation, the AEIP Scholars Programme represents an excellent platform for growth. Eligible scholars are encouraged to prepare their strongest research abstracts and submit their applications before 31 August 2026 . Visit the OFY website for more F ellowship Opportunities . title: France-South Africa Scholarship Programme 2027: Fully Funded Master’s and PhD Scholarships to Study in France for Students from South Africa, Lesotho, and Malawi
summary: The 2027 France-South Africa Scholarship Programme is officially open for applications, offering an exceptional opportunity for eligible students from South Africa, Lesotho, and Malawi to pursue Master s and PhD degrees in France . This prestigious scholarship programme supports talented students who wish to undertake postgraduate studies at French universities and higher education institutions beginning in September 2027 . The initiative strengthens academic cooperation between France and Southern African countries while promoting research, innovation, international collaboration, and the development of highly skilled professionals across numerous disciplines. Students interested in obtaining world-class education in France are encouraged to submit their applications before the closing date. Applications are currently open and must be submitted no later than 8 October 2026 at 23:59 (South Africa Time). About the France-South Africa Scholarship Programme The France-South Africa Scholarship Programme is designed to provide deserving students with an opportunity to pursue postgraduate studies in France. The programme specifically targets students who intend to enroll in accredited French universities or higher education institutions for either a Master s degree or a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) . The scholarship is part of France s broader commitment to strengthening educational partnerships with African countries while supporting academic excellence, research collaboration, innovation, and capacity building. Successful applicants will commence their studies in September 2027 , following participation in preparatory online French language courses. Why Study in France? France remains one of the world s leading destinations for higher education because of its: Internationally recognized universities Excellent research facilities Strong academic reputation Affordable higher education compared to many Western countries Rich cultural heritage Diverse international student community Strong links between universities and industry Opportunities for innovation and entrepreneurship Studying in France also enables students to gain international exposure while building valuable professional and academic networks. Who Can Apply? The scholarship programme is open exclusively to applicants who hold citizenship of: South Africa Lesotho Malawi Applicants must intend to begin their postgraduate studies in France in September 2027 . Available Degree Levels Applicants may apply to pursue: Master s Degree PhD (Doctoral Degree) The programme supports studies at recognized French universities and higher education institutions. Fields of Study Applications are accepted from all academic disciplines . However, priority consideration will be given to applicants pursuing programmes in: Science Technology Engineering Mathematics (STEM) The programme also recognizes related fields within: Humanities Social Sciences This means applicants from non-STEM disciplines remain eligible to apply, although STEM-related applications may receive additional consideration during the selection process. French Language Preparation Because academic calendars differ between Southern Hemisphere countries and France, scholarship recipients will participate in online French language courses before travelling. Successful applicants will receive: Online French language training Courses delivered by the Alliances Françaises network Training period from February to July 2027 These courses are intended to help students integrate academically and socially before arriving in France. Benefits of the Scholarship While the announcement does not specify financial details, the programme offers successful applicants the opportunity to: Study at prestigious French universities Access internationally recognized postgraduate education Receive French language preparation before departure Join international academic and research communities Build global professional networks Enhance research and career prospects Experience French culture and higher education Applicants should consult the official programme rulebook for detailed scholarship benefits and funding information. Important Resources for Applicants Applicants are strongly encouraged to review the following resources before submitting their applications: France-South Africa Scholarship Programme Rulebook Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) Campus France South Africa website Information about French universities Available study programmes Admission guidance Students who require assistance selecting an appropriate programme are encouraged to contact Campus France South Africa for academic advice. Selection Process The scholarship selection process follows several stages: Submission of applications Eligibility review Interviews for shortlisted candidates Final selection Announcement of successful candidates French language preparation Departure to France Applicants selected for interviews will be contacted individually. Important Timeline Applications Open 21 July 2026 Application Deadline 8 October 2026 at 23:59 (South Africa Time) Information Webinar August 2026 Applicants should follow Campus France South Africa s social media platforms for webinar details. Interviews November 2026 Eligible candidates will be invited for interviews. Announcement of Shortlisted Candidates Beginning of December 2026 French Language Training February – July 2027 Online language preparation through Alliances Françaises. Departure to France September 2027 Successful candidates begin their postgraduate studies in France. Important Notes for Applicants Applicants should keep the following in mind: Read the scholarship rulebook carefully before applying. Ensure all required documents are submitted before the deadline. Late applications are unlikely to be accepted. Scholarship recipients and shortlisted candidates will be contacted individually. Due to the high volume of applications, follow-up inquiries from applicants will not receive responses. If you have not received any communication from the scholarship panel by February 2027 , you should consider your application unsuccessful. Decisions made by the Scholarship Panel are final and cannot be appealed. Tips for Preparing a Strong Application To maximize your chances of success: Begin your application early. Carefully research suitable universities and programmes in France. Prepare a compelling motivation letter. Ensure your academic records are complete and accurate. Clearly explain how your proposed studies align with your academic and career goals. Verify that all supporting documents meet programme requirements. Submit your application well before the deadline to avoid technical issues. APPLY HERE Why You Should Apply The France-South Africa Scholarship Programme provides an outstanding opportunity for ambitious students seeking internationally recognized postgraduate education in France. Beyond earning a prestigious Master s or PhD degree, recipients gain access to world-class research environments, international collaborations, cultural exchange, and valuable language training that prepares them for academic success. Whether your ambitions lie in scientific research, technological innovation, engineering, social sciences, or the humanities, this scholarship offers a pathway toward advanced education and global career opportunities. Students who meet the eligibility requirements are encouraged to begin preparing their applications as early as possible to ensure they submit a complete and competitive application before the deadline. Visit HERE to learn more about the France-South Africa Scholarship Programme 2027 Conclusion The France-South Africa Scholarship Programme 2027 represents a significant opportunity for talented postgraduate students from South Africa, Lesotho, and Malawi to pursue advanced studies in France. By supporting Master s and PhD candidates across a broad range of disciplines, the programme promotes academic excellence, international collaboration, and long-term professional development. Prospective applicants should carefully review all programme guidelines, research suitable institutions and study programmes, and submit complete applications before 8 October 2026 at 23:59 (South Africa Time) . Early preparation, attention to detail, and a strong academic profile will significantly improve the likelihood of success. title: GEDA Small Grants 2026–2027: Apply for Up to USD $15,000 to Advance Gender and Environment Data for Climate Action
summary: GEDA Small Grants applications for the 2026–2027 funding cycle are now open, offering organizations an opportunity to secure grants of up to USD $15,000 to support innovative projects at the intersection of gender equality, environmental sustainability, climate action, and data-driven research . Through the Gender and Environment Data Alliance (GEDA), this initiative aims to strengthen the collection, analysis, and application of gender-environment data while promoting inclusive, evidence-based climate policies and empowering locally led, feminist, and community-driven solutions. Successful organizations will not only receive financial support but will also have the opportunity to participate in the GEDA Data Fellowship , a six-month capacity-building program designed to enhance skills in data collection, analysis, research communication, and policy advocacy. Together, the grant and fellowship provide a unique platform for organizations to amplify their impact, influence climate and environmental decision-making, and contribute to more equitable and gender-responsive environmental governance worldwide. What is the GEDA Small Grants Program? The Gender and Environment Data Alliance (GEDA) is an international initiative dedicated to improving the availability, accessibility, understanding, and use of high-quality data at the intersection of gender equality and environmental sustainability . GEDA works to: Improve access to gender and environmental data. Identify important knowledge gaps. Strengthen evidence-based climate and environmental policymaking. Promote gender-just approaches to environmental governance. Support locally led and feminist research methodologies. Elevate underrepresented voices in climate and environmental decision-making. Through the 2026–2027 Small Grants Program, GEDA aims to support organizations that can generate meaningful knowledge and practical solutions for climate and environmental challenges affecting diverse communities worldwide. Funding Available For the 2026–2027 funding cycle, GEDA will award at least eight (8) grants . Each selected organization will receive: Funding between USD $10,000 and USD $15,000 Grant disbursement beginning in September/October 2026 Project implementation period of up to one year Activities concluding by October 2027 The funding is intended to directly support projects involving gender-environment data production, research, analysis, dissemination, advocacy, and capacity development. GEDA Small Grants Program Objectives The grants are designed to contribute to two major objectives: 1. Strengthen Gender-Transformative Climate Action Projects should contribute toward: Better environmental and climate policies Improved programming Stronger financing decisions Inclusive planning processes Evidence-based decision-making through improved gender-environment data. 2. Amplify Marginalized Voices GEDA seeks projects that: Support excluded communities Promote feminist research Encourage participatory methodologies Build locally owned knowledge Increase visibility of community-generated evidence This reflects GEDA s commitment to equitable and inclusive climate governance. What Types of Projects Will Be Supported? GEDA welcomes a wide range of innovative projects centered on gender and environmental data. Examples include: Data Collection Projects Applicants may conduct: Community surveys Household data collection Environmental monitoring Gender-focused climate assessments Participatory mapping Indigenous knowledge documentation Quantitative or qualitative research Projects are encouraged to adopt participatory and locally led approaches. Data Analysis Funding may support: Statistical analysis Gender impact assessments Climate vulnerability studies Environmental justice research Data visualization Policy-oriented analysis Capacity Building Organizations may also use the funding to: Train researchers Develop learning materials Build institutional data capacity Create toolkits Deliver workshops Produce training modules on feminist data methodologies Advocacy and Knowledge Dissemination Projects can focus on: Policy advocacy Public awareness campaigns Creative communication approaches Publishing research findings Disseminating existing evidence Encouraging wider use of gender-environment data Importantly, projects do not have to generate new datasets to qualify. Existing research may be strengthened, synthesized, or translated into practical resources for policymakers and practitioners. Priority Research Areas While projects covering any gender-environment topic are welcome, GEDA has identified several priority areas connected to the recently adopted Belém Gender Action Plan (GAP) under the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC). Priority themes include: Health in the context of gender and climate change Gender-based violence linked to climate change Care work and climate change However, projects outside these themes remain fully eligible for funding. Learn more about how data is integrated into the Belém GAP here . GEDA Data Fellowship Every funded organization will have the opportunity to nominate up to two individuals to participate in the prestigious GEDA Data Fellowship . The fellowship is delivered by Data4Change and includes: Six months of structured learning Professional mentorship Peer learning opportunities Practical training in data analysis Communication skills development Audience-specific storytelling Development of advocacy materials The fellowship is intended to strengthen each organization s ability to transform research into impactful communication that supports policy change and advocacy goals. Regional Focus The 2026–2027 funding round has a significant emphasis on the Indo-Pacific region . Out of the eight grants: Six grants are reserved for projects within the Indo-Pacific focusing on the intersection of: Gender Equality Disability Social Inclusion (GEDSI) Climate adaptation Climate resilience Two grants are open to all eligible GEDA members globally, although organizations based in the Global South will receive preference. Eligible Countries in the Indo-Pacific Priority Window Eligible Indo-Pacific countries include: Pacific Fiji Samoa Tonga Vanuatu Papua New Guinea Solomon Islands Kiribati Tuvalu Nauru Palau Marshall Islands Federated States of Micronesia Niue Tokelau Southeast Asia Cambodia Indonesia Laos Myanmar Philippines Timor-Leste Vietnam South and Central Asia Afghanistan Bangladesh Bhutan Maldives Mongolia Nepal Pakistan Sri Lanka Eligibility Requirements Applicants must meet the following conditions: Be a GEDA Member, Core Partner, or Data Advisory Group (DAG) member. Organizations in the Indo-Pacific that are not currently GEDA members may also apply and will be invited to join GEDA if selected. DAG members may partner with organizations that are not currently GEDA members. Steering Committee members may apply but must recuse themselves from the selection process. Preference will be given to organizations or consultancy firms based in the Global South. Projects implemented at the local or national level are strongly encouraged. Expectations for Successful Grantees Organizations selected for funding will be expected to: Participate in informal bi-monthly check-in meetings with the GEDA Secretariat. Submit a brief narrative report at the end of the project. Submit a basic financial report upon project completion. Complete reporting by October 2027 using templates provided by GEDA. How to Apply Applications must be submitted through the official Airtable application form , with a Microsoft Word version available for accessibility. The application requests: Organizational information Project overview Proposed activities Timeline Budget Expected impact Monitoring indicators GEDA encourages applicants to write authentically and emphasizes that perfect grammar is not required. While AI-generated responses are not prohibited, applicants are encouraged to use their own voice and lived experience. Organizations needing translation or accessibility support may contact Jay Saeed ( jahanara@wedo.org ) for assistance. APPLY NOW Important Dates Applications Open: July 16, 2026 Information Sessions: ○ Option A : Monday, July 27: 8 AM ET/noon UTC/1 PM WAT/ 3PM EAT ○ Option B : Tuesday, July 28: 8 PM ET = Wednesday, July 29 midnight UTC/8AM SGT/10AM AEST/noon NZST Application Deadline: August 14, 2026 Announcement of Successful Applicants: Week of September 14, 2026 Grant Disbursement: By October 2, 2026 Why Organizations Should Apply The GEDA Small Grants Program offers much more than financial assistance. It provides an opportunity to: Secure up to USD $15,000 in funding. Join a global network advancing gender and environmental justice. Strengthen organizational research and data capabilities. Receive mentorship through the GEDA Data Fellowship. Influence climate policy through evidence-based advocacy. Promote locally led and feminist research methodologies. Build partnerships with international experts and practitioners. Increase the visibility and impact of community-driven environmental initiatives. Conclusion The GEDA Small Grants 2026–2027 program represents a valuable opportunity for organizations committed to advancing gender equality and environmental sustainability through high-quality data and evidence. By combining grant funding with specialized fellowship training, GEDA is empowering organizations to produce meaningful research, strengthen advocacy efforts, and contribute to more inclusive climate policies worldwide. Whether your organization focuses on climate resilience, gender-responsive policymaking, disability inclusion, environmental justice, community research, or participatory data collection, this initiative offers the resources and global platform needed to amplify your impact. Interested organizations should begin preparing their applications early and ensure they submit all required information before the August 14, 2026 deadline. Visit the OFY website for more Grant Opportunities . title: Skills & Innovation Academy Ghana: Free Pre-Employment Training Connecting Graduates with SME Jobs in Ghana
summary: Finding meaningful employment after graduation remains one of the biggest challenges facing young professionals in Ghana. While thousands of graduates enter the labor market each year equipped with academic qualifications, many employers continue to report difficulties finding candidates with the practical and workplace-ready skills required for immediate employment. To bridge this gap, the Skills Innovation Academy , supported by the German Development Cooperation, has introduced an innovative initiative that prepares graduates for employment while helping Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) access qualified, job-ready talent. The Academy offers free pre-employment training tailored specifically to the real workforce needs of Ghanaian SMEs. The initiative enables businesses to recruit skilled graduates while giving young professionals practical skills that significantly improve their employability. The program forms part of the Special Initiative Decent Work for a Just Transition , operating under the Invest for Jobs brand and funded by Germany s Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ). Implementation is led by Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH , with implementation support from MDOZ Company Limited through consulting services. This initiative represents a practical solution to addressing youth unemployment, strengthening SME competitiveness, and promoting sustainable economic development across Ghana. About the Skills Innovation Academy The Skills Innovation Academy is designed to close the gap between education and employment by ensuring graduates possess the exact competencies employers are actively seeking. Unlike conventional training programs that rely on generic curricula, this Academy developed its training after conducting a comprehensive enterprise needs assessment among Ghanaian SMEs. This assessment identified the skills businesses expect to need over the next one to two years, allowing the Academy to build an industry-driven curriculum that directly reflects employer demand. As a result, graduates complete training equipped with relevant technical expertise, digital capabilities, workplace competencies, and professional attitudes required to succeed from their very first day on the job. Why the Program Matters Small and Medium Enterprises play a crucial role in Ghana s economy. They generate employment, stimulate innovation, and contribute significantly to economic growth. However, many SMEs continue to face challenges in recruiting candidates with practical experience and industry-relevant skills. Research conducted by the Skills Innovation Academy revealed that, alongside access to finance and markets, access to qualified human resources remains one of the greatest growth opportunities for Ghanaian SMEs. The Academy therefore focuses on producing graduates who can immediately contribute to business productivity while reducing recruitment and onboarding costs for employers. What Makes This Program Unique? The Skills Innovation Academy distinguishes itself through its employer-centered approach. Instead of offering generalized training, every aspect of the curriculum has been developed based on the actual hiring needs of Ghanaian businesses. The training emphasizes practical application, workplace readiness, and future-focused competencies. Key features include: Employer-informed curriculum Free pre-employment training Industry-specific technical skills Digital skills development Artificial Intelligence (AI) training Workplace safety education Resource-efficient production methods Cleaner production practices Soft skills for professional success Direct connection with hiring SMEs Training Areas Participants receive comprehensive training across multiple disciplines designed to improve their employment prospects. 1. Sector-Specific Technical Skills Graduates gain practical knowledge tailored to industries where SMEs are actively recruiting. These technical competencies are based on current and anticipated market demand. 2. Digital Skills Digital literacy has become essential across virtually every industry. The Academy equips graduates with modern digital competencies that improve workplace productivity and efficiency. 3. Artificial Intelligence (AI) Recognizing the increasing importance of AI in business operations, the Academy introduces participants to AI tools and technologies relevant to today s workplace. Graduates learn how emerging technologies can improve productivity and support business growth. 4. Resource-Efficient and Cleaner Production Sustainability is becoming increasingly important for businesses worldwide. Participants are trained in methods that promote efficient resource utilization while reducing environmental impact. 5. Workplace Safety Understanding workplace health and safety standards helps graduates contribute to safer working environments while meeting employer expectations. 6. Soft Skills Development Technical knowledge alone is often insufficient for long-term career success. The Academy therefore emphasizes employability skills including: Professional communication Teamwork Problem-solving Time management Critical thinking Adaptability Professional ethics Leadership potential Customer service Workplace professionalism These competencies enable graduates to integrate quickly into professional environments. Benefits for Graduates Successful participants stand to gain numerous advantages through the Skills Innovation Academy. title: UNICEF Gender-Responsive Social Protection E-Course: Self-Paced Training for Practitioners and Development Professionals
summary: UNICEF is offering a self-paced online course on Gender-Responsive Social Protection , designed to help practitioners, development professionals and government partners understand how gender shapes access to opportunity, security, services and well-being throughout a person’s life. The course introduces the principles and practical application of Gender-Responsive Social Protection, commonly abbreviated as GRSP. It examines how social protection policies and programmes can be designed, delivered, monitored and improved so that they respond to gender-related risks, prevent exclusion and promote dignity, equality and empowerment. Through interactive exercises, decision-based scenarios, videos, case studies and reflection activities, learners will explore how gender-responsive approaches can improve social protection systems for women, girls and other groups facing intersecting forms of disadvantage. The activity is delivered online in English and takes approximately two hours to complete. It is open for self-enrollment, and no application deadline is stated. About the UNICEF Gender-Responsive Social Protection Course Gender-Responsive Social Protection is an approach that recognizes that women, men, girls, boys and gender-diverse individuals may experience poverty, vulnerability and access to public services differently. Gender can affect: Who performs unpaid care work Who has access to identification documents Who controls household income Who is able to travel safely to collect payments Who receives information about available programmes Who is formally registered for benefits Who faces discrimination or exclusion Who can use grievance and complaints systems Who is most exposed to economic, environmental or social shocks A social protection programme may appear neutral while still producing unequal outcomes. For example, a payment system may technically be open to everyone but remain inaccessible to women who lack bank accounts, identification documents, mobile phones, transport or control over household finances. The course helps learners identify these barriers and consider how programmes can be adjusted to promote fairer and more effective outcomes. Although the activity is categorized as an advanced e-course, the description presents it as a foundational introduction to Gender-Responsive Social Protection. It therefore provides core concepts while also introducing practical frameworks and tools that can be applied in programme design, delivery, monitoring and advocacy. The Story-Based Learning Approach The course follows the story of Mia , an adolescent girl living in a flood-prone coastal town. Her daily experiences illustrate how gender roles, safety concerns, time pressures and access to documentation can influence whether someone receives social protection support. As learners progress through the course, they are encouraged to consider questions such as: What barriers make it difficult for Mia to access support? How do household and community expectations affect her choices? Does she have the documents required for registration? Can she safely reach registration or payment locations? Does she have access to information about available services? Are programme staff aware of the gender-related risks she faces? How could the system be redesigned to serve her more effectively? Mia’s experience provides a practical thread connecting the course modules. It shows that removing barriers for adolescent girls and other excluded groups can improve programme accessibility and effectiveness for the wider population. Why Gender Matters in Social Protection Social protection systems are intended to reduce poverty, manage risks and support people during periods of vulnerability. These systems may include cash transfers, social insurance, public employment programmes, food assistance, child benefits, pensions and other forms of support. However, people do not experience vulnerability in identical ways. Gender-related inequalities may influence: Employment opportunities Income security Ownership of assets Access to education Exposure to violence Unpaid care responsibilities Mobility Digital access Financial inclusion Participation in decision-making Access to public institutions These inequalities can become more severe during crises such as floods, conflict, displacement, economic shocks or public-health emergencies. A gender-responsive approach does not simply add women or girls to an existing programme. It examines how the entire system operates and whether its design, implementation and monitoring address gender-based barriers. Course Learning Objectives By the end of the UNICEF Gender-Responsive Social Protection course, learners should be able to achieve the following objectives. 1. Understand Core Concepts Participants will learn to define and distinguish concepts including: Gender equality Gender equity Intersectionality Social protection Gender responsiveness Inclusion Empowerment Understanding these terms is important because they shape how programmes identify inequalities and develop appropriate responses. 2. Explain Why Gender Matters Learners will examine how gender affects risks and vulnerabilities at different stages of life. These stages may include: Childhood Adolescence Working age Parenthood Older age Participants will consider how expectations, discrimination and unequal access to resources can influence a person’s ability to benefit from social protection. 3. Apply Gender Analysis The course introduces gender-analysis frameworks and tools that can be used to assess whether a social protection programme is responsive to the needs of different groups. Gender analysis may examine: Who has access to resources Who participates in decision-making Who performs paid and unpaid work Who controls income or benefits Who faces safety risks Who is excluded from registration or payments How gender interacts with disability, age, migration status, poverty or location 4. Design Gender-Responsive Interventions Learners will be introduced to a structured, step-by-step approach for designing or adapting social protection interventions. This may include: Identifying gender-related risks and barriers Understanding the affected population Reviewing the existing programme design Selecting practical adjustments Consulting affected communities Integrating safeguards Developing indicators Monitoring results and unintended consequences 5. Improve Delivery Systems A well-designed policy can still exclude people if its delivery systems are inaccessible or unsafe. The course examines key delivery stages, including: Outreach and communication Identification and eligibility assessment Registration Enrollment Payments Referral services Complaints and grievance mechanisms Learners will consider how each stage can be improved to promote equity and reduce the risk of exclusion, discrimination or harm. 6. Develop Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Plans Participants will learn how to develop a basic gender-responsive monitoring, evaluation and learning plan. This may involve: Selecting measurable indicators Collecting gender-disaggregated data Monitoring programme accessibility Assessing whether benefits reach intended groups Identifying unintended harm Gathering feedback from participants Using findings to improve programme delivery Gender-responsive monitoring should move beyond counting how many women or girls participate. It should examine whether the programme changes access, safety, decision-making, time use, income security or other relevant outcomes. 7. Advocate for Policy and System-Level Change The course also helps learners understand how evidence, partnerships and inclusive stakeholder engagement can support broader policy change. Effective advocacy may involve collaboration among: Government ministries Social protection agencies Civil society organisations Women’s rights organisations Youth groups International organisations Donors Researchers Private-sector partners Communities receiving support 8. Demonstrate and Continue Learning Participants will complete lesson-level knowledge checks and a final assessment. They will also be introduced to tools and resources that can support continued application after the course. Course Structure The UNICEF Gender-Responsive Social Protection e-course consists of five modules. Module 1: Understanding Gender and Social Protection The first module introduces the relationship between gender and social protection. Learners explore concepts such as equality, equity and intersectionality while examining how gender-related inequalities affect vulnerability and access to support. Module 2: Designing Gender-Responsive Social Protection This module focuses on programme design. Participants learn how to apply gender analysis and use a structured approach to develop or adapt social protection interventions. Module 3: Delivering Gender-Responsive Social Protection The third module examines delivery systems. It considers how outreach, registration, enrollment, payment arrangements and grievance mechanisms can either promote inclusion or reinforce existing inequalities. Module 4: Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning for GRSP This module introduces gender-responsive monitoring, evaluation and learning. Learners examine how indicators, data and participant feedback can be used to assess whether a programme is achieving equitable outcomes. Module 5: Advocacy for Gender-Responsive Social Protection The final module focuses on advocacy, collaboration and policy change. It considers how practitioners can use evidence and stakeholder engagement to strengthen gender responsiveness across social protection systems. Course Methodology The course uses a self-paced, learner-centred methodology based on modular microlearning. Learning activities include: Story-based scenarios Decision-based exercises Interactive videos Practical case studies Reflection activities Knowledge checks Instant feedback A final assessment Tools for practical application The course is grounded in adult-learning principles and has been designed to support inclusive and accessible learning. Its practical structure allows participants to connect theoretical concepts with real-world social protection challenges. Course Duration and Format The estimated completion time is: Approximately two hours The course is: Fully online Self-paced Delivered in English Open for self-enrollment Divided into five modules Because it is self-paced, learners can progress through the materials according to their schedules. The listing does not state whether participants must complete all modules in one sitting or whether a certificate is awarded. Learners should confirm certification and completion requirements on the enrollment platform. Who Is the Course Designed For? The course has a broad professional audience. It is suitable for: UNICEF Personnel Country office staff Regional office staff Headquarters personnel Centres of Excellence personnel Consultants Interns Volunteers Goodwill ambassadors Board members National Committee representatives Government and Public-Sector Professionals The course may be particularly relevant to officials working in: Social protection Social welfare Gender equality Labour Finance Education Health Child protection Disaster risk management Humanitarian response Monitoring and evaluation Public policy Civil Society and Development Partners Non-UNICEF participants may include: Civil society organisations International NGOs Local NGOs Foundations Donors Researchers Universities Advocacy organisations Private-sector partners Social-policy professionals Gender specialists The course is especially relevant to people involved in programme design, implementation, delivery, evaluation or policy advocacy. Areas of Professional Relevance The e-course may support work in areas including: Gender equality Social protection systems Women’s empowerment Adolescent programming Child protection Migration Social inclusion Economic and social policy Risk-informed programming Climate resilience Advocacy Capacity development Monitoring and evaluation Programme operations Professionals working in crisis-prone or climate-vulnerable environments may find the content particularly useful because the course illustrates how shocks can interact with existing gender inequalities. Competency Developed The course is connected to the competency: Demonstrates self-awareness and ethical awareness This competency is relevant because gender-responsive programming requires practitioners to reflect critically on assumptions, power relationships and the potential unintended consequences of programme decisions. It also requires professionals to consider: Whose voices are included Whose needs are overlooked How data is collected and used Whether interventions create additional risks Whether programmes respect dignity and agency How affected communities participate in decisions How to Enroll The course is open to self-enrollment. Prospective learners should access the course page and select the enrollment option provided on the platform. Before beginning, participants may need to create or sign in to a learning-platform account. The listing does not mention an application form, competitive selection process or enrollment fee. ENROLL HERE Application Deadline No application or enrollment deadline is stated. The course appears to remain available for self-enrollment. However, course availability can change, so interested learners should register while the activity remains open. Course and learner-management inquiries are directed to Shreyasi Jha. Learners should use the contact options provided on the official course platform when requesting technical assistance or clarification. Conclusion The UNICEF Gender-Responsive Social Protection e-course provides a practical introduction to designing and delivering social protection systems that respond to gender-related inequalities. Through the story of an adolescent girl living in a flood-prone community, learners examine how safety, time, documentation, social expectations and access to services influence whether people receive support. The course moves from foundational concepts to practical programme design, delivery, monitoring and advocacy. Its five-module structure equips participants to identify barriers, assess programme responsiveness and propose improvements that promote equality, dignity and inclusion. With an estimated duration of approximately two hours, a self-paced format and open enrolment, the course is accessible to UNICEF personnel, government officials, civil society partners and other professionals working in gender equality, social protection and inclusive policy. Applicants interested in this track should answer all application questions truthfully and provide any relevant teaching, tutoring, academic, or competition-related experience. Benefits of the ATDP Fellowship Program Selected fellows will receive several professional and developmental benefits during the six-month program. Six months of structured professional experience The fellowship provides an extended period of workplace exposure, allowing participants to develop their skills gradually and gain meaningful experience over six months. This duration may enable fellows to participate in projects from their initial planning stages through implementation, monitoring, and completion. Paid fellowship with monthly stipends Fellows will receive monthly stipends during the program. The exact stipend amount has not been stated in the provided application information. Applicants should not assume a particular amount unless it is formally communicated by the organizers. Hands-on training Participants will receive practical training intended to strengthen their ability to perform professional responsibilities. Hands-on training may involve supervised assignments, workplace tools, digital platforms, research tasks, project support, administrative duties, customer engagement, educational initiatives, or other responsibilities connected to the fellow’s assigned area. Mentorship from experienced professionals Selected fellows will have access to professional mentorship. This provides an opportunity to learn from individuals with practical experience in their respective fields. Mentorship can help fellows: Set professional development goals Improve the quality of their work Address weaknesses Build confidence Develop stronger workplace habits Understand professional standards Make informed career decisions Certificate upon successful completion Fellows who successfully complete the program will receive a certificate. The certificate may serve as formal evidence of participation and completion and can be included in a curriculum vitae, professional portfolio, job application, or online professional profile. Potential internship opportunity Participants may have an opportunity to undertake an internship with ATDP or one of its partner organizations. The wording of the announcement indicates that this is an opportunity rather than a guaranteed placement for every fellow. Internship availability may depend on performance, organizational needs, available placements, and the selection decisions of ATDP or its partner institutions. Exposure to professional networks Through interactions with mentors, staff members, partner organizations, and other fellows, participants may expand their professional networks. These connections can be valuable for learning, collaboration, referrals, professional guidance, and future career opportunities. Improved employability The combination of practical experience, mentorship, digital skills, workplace exposure, and certification may help fellows become more competitive when applying for future jobs, internships, training programs, or further development opportunities. Eligibility Requirements for the ATDP Fellowship 2026 Applicants must meet the following requirements. Age requirement Applicants must be between 20 and 30 years old . The available announcement does not explain whether applicants who are exactly 20 or exactly 30 are eligible, but the standard meaning of the stated age range indicates that both ages are included. Location requirement Applicants must live within Accra, Ghana . This is an important condition because the fellowship is Accra-based. Applicants should apply only if they currently live in Accra or can meet the program’s attendance and location requirements. The announcement does not state that relocation assistance, accommodation, or transportation support will be provided. Digital proficiency Applicants must be proficient in the use of: Microsoft Office Suite; or Google Workspace Relevant applications may include: Microsoft Word Microsoft Excel Microsoft PowerPoint Microsoft Outlook Google Docs Google Sheets Google Slides Google Drive Gmail Google Meet Google Calendar Applicants should be prepared to demonstrate their ability to use digital productivity tools for communication, document preparation, recordkeeping, presentations, reporting, scheduling, and collaboration. Availability for the full program Applicants must be able to commit to the full six-month duration of the fellowship. Candidates should consider their academic schedule, employment responsibilities, personal commitments, travel plans, and other obligations before applying. Interest in professional development Although not presented as a formal technical requirement, the program is intended for passionate, driven, and ambitious individuals who are willing to learn and contribute. Applicants should demonstrate genuine motivation and a clear interest in gaining practical experience. Is a University Degree Required? The available fellowship announcement does not specify a mandatory university degree, diploma, academic discipline, grade point average, or minimum level of education. Applicants should therefore avoid assuming that a particular academic qualification is required unless additional instructions appear inside the application form or are communicated by the organizers. Candidates should accurately provide their educational background, professional training, certifications, and relevant experience when completing the application. Application Process Interested applicants should complete the official ATDP Fellowship application form. The application is expected to take approximately five minutes to complete. Applicants should follow these steps: Review the fellowship areas and identify the area most closely connected to their interests and capabilities. Confirm that they are between 20 and 30 years old. Confirm that they live within Accra. Ensure that they can commit to the full six-month program. Prepare accurate personal, educational, and professional information. Complete all required questions in the application form. Upload any documents requested through the form. Review all responses carefully. Submit the application before 30 July 2026. Retain any submission confirmation received after applying. The Google Form indicates that the applicant’s Google Account name, email address, and profile photo may be recorded when files are uploaded and the form is submitted. Applicants should therefore make sure they are signed in using an appropriate and accessible email account. Official Application Link Applications can be submitted through the official Google Form: Click HERE to apply. Applicants may also access the form by scanning the QR code provided on the official fellowship advertisement. Application Deadline The deadline to apply for the ATDP Fellowship Program 2026 is: 30 July 2026 Applicants are strongly advised not to wait until the final day. Submitting early can reduce the risk of internet problems, incomplete uploads, login difficulties, or last-minute errors. Applications submitted after the deadline may not be considered unless the organizers formally announce an extension. Selection Process Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted for the next stage of the selection process. This means that submitting an application does not automatically guarantee: Shortlisting Selection Participation Internship placement Employment Future engagement with a partner organization Applicants should provide clear, accurate, and relevant responses that demonstrate their suitability for the program. The available announcement does not specify: The number of available fellowship positions Whether interviews will be conducted The expected program start date The amount of the monthly stipend Daily or weekly working hours Whether the fellowship is fully on-site, hybrid, or partially remote Whether transportation or accommodation support will be provided Whether all fellows will receive an internship placement Shortlisted candidates should request clarification on these matters if they are invited to the next stage. How to Prepare a Strong ATDP Fellowship Application Applicants can improve the quality of their applications by following the guidance below. Select the most relevant fellowship area Choose a fellowship area that genuinely matches your interests, education, skills, or prior experience. For example: Applicants with technology or digital learning interests may consider EdTech and Artificial Intelligence. Applicants with communication and commercial interests may consider Business Development and Customer Service. Applicants with accounting, recordkeeping, office management, or organizational interests may consider Administration and Finance. Applicants interested in scholarships and academic development may consider Global Scholars. Applicants with teaching, tutoring, coaching, or academic competition experience may consider Olympiad Certified Teaching Fellow. Demonstrate motivation with specific examples Avoid generic statements such as “I am passionate” without supporting evidence. Instead, explain: What you have already done in the relevant area What skills you want to develop Why the fellowship matters to your career How you can contribute to ATDP What impact you hope to make Highlight relevant digital skills Since Microsoft Office or Google Workspace proficiency is required, applicants should mention practical experience using these tools. Examples may include: Preparing reports in Microsoft Word Managing data in Microsoft Excel Creating presentations in PowerPoint Collaborating through Google Docs Organizing information in Google Sheets Managing files through Google Drive Scheduling meetings through Google Calendar Keep information accurate Do not exaggerate qualifications, employment experience, certifications, or technical expertise. Application information may be reviewed or verified during the selection process. Review the application before submission Check: Spelling Grammar Contact details Uploaded documents Selected fellowship area Educational information Employment information Availability Motivation responses A carefully completed application creates a stronger professional impression. Important Considerations Before Applying Prospective applicants should consider the following points: The fellowship is based in Accra. Applicants must be between 20 and 30 years old. Participants must commit to six months. The fellowship is paid, but the stipend amount has not been disclosed. Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted. An internship opportunity may be available, but it is not described as guaranteed for every participant. Limited fellowship spots are available. The deadline is 30 July 2026. Applicants should use accurate contact information that they check regularly. Why the ATDP Fellowship May Be Valuable Many young professionals face difficulty entering the workforce because employers often require practical experience, while early-career applicants may not yet have had an opportunity to gain that experience. The ATDP Fellowship may help address this challenge by combining workplace exposure, mentorship, skills development, financial support, and certification. The program may be particularly useful for applicants who: Want to gain their first structured professional experience Need practical exposure after completing academic studies Want to improve their digital and administrative skills Are exploring careers in education, business, technology, finance, or customer service Want mentorship from experienced professionals Need stronger evidence of professional competence Want to build a professional network Are interested in potential internship opportunities However, applicants should evaluate the opportunity based on their own career goals, availability, location, and preferred fellowship area. Frequently Asked Questions Is the ATDP Fellowship paid? Yes. The announcement describes it as a six-month paid fellowship and states that fellows will receive monthly stipends. What is the stipend amount? The stipend amount has not been stated in the provided application materials. How long does the fellowship last? The fellowship lasts for six months. Where is the program based? The program is based in Accra, Ghana. What is the eligible age range? Applicants must be between 20 and 30 years old. Can applicants outside Accra apply? Will every applicant receive a response? No. Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted for the next stage. When is the deadline? The application deadline is 30 July 2026. Conclusion The ATDP Fellowship Program 2026 offers a valuable six-month paid professional development opportunity for young people living in Accra who want to strengthen their practical skills and gain workplace experience. With fellowship areas covering EdTech and Artificial Intelligence, Business Development and Customer Service, Administration and Finance, Global Scholars, and Olympiad Certified Teaching, the program accommodates applicants with a range of professional interests. Selected fellows will benefit from hands-on training, mentorship, monthly stipends, certification, and possible internship exposure through ATDP or one of its partner organizations.
